titulo: A1 review and mock test: The most common A1 mistakes and writing

aula.objetivo: Review the whole of A1 in one map, practice reading, listening, writing and speaking, fix the most common mistakes English speakers make, and take an original practice test with a commented answer key, covering lessons 1 through 17.

sessao.titulo: The most common A1 mistakes and writing

blocos.explicacao: Read each pair out loud: first the wrong version, then the right one, then the rule. Mark the mistakes you still make and go back to the lesson named in the explanation.

erros.motivo: Age is said with «tener», not with «ser» (lesson 3).
After a verb, use «mucho»; «muy» only comes before an adjective or adverb (lesson 4).
A person as the object calls for the personal «a» (lesson 4).

erros.errado: [misto] Hay el libro en la mesa.
erros.certo: [misto] Hay un libro en la mesa. / El libro está en la mesa.
erros.motivo: «Hay» introduces something new, with an indefinite article; something already known uses «está» (lessons 5 and 10).
The place where someone is calls for «estar» (lesson 10).
Plural clock times take «son»; only «es la una» is singular (lesson 9).
The reflexive pronoun is required and comes first (lesson 14).
The demonstrative agrees with the noun (lesson 15).
The verb agrees with the thing that's liked (lesson 16).
Feelings like cold, hunger, or thirst use «tener», not «ser» — the reverse of English «I am cold».

blocos.enunciado: Write a short email (about 60 words) to a friend who lives in Spain: introduce yourself, say where you live and what you do, describe your morning routine, tell them what you did today, and invite them for the weekend. Then read it out loud.
Write three mistakes you still make at A1, with the correct form, and state the rule for each one.
